title: bittorrent: decode extension bits in handshake
description:
Adds decoding of the extension bits in the BitTorrent handshake message.
This covers the bits that I have both seen in the wild and could find a
reference for. New official extensions are handled with the extended
handshake, indicated by the extension.ltep bit, so this bitfield is
likely to remain fairly static.

Relevant documents are BEP 4, 5, 6, 10 and 52. In addition the info on
reserved[5] |= 0x08 comes from libtorrent commit 784f978f77.

The full set of bits I've seen are 0xe5780000001f0015, but the unmatched
bits are all rare with one or more bits appearing in 0.2% of handshakes.

AI-Assisted: yes (Qwen3.6 for review)

notes.body: You now leave a whole bunch of bits un-dissected. It's good practice to find a way the show these as well, so that it becomes obvious when 'new' bits are being used.

added 3 commits
  • 32e0c320...a44c8dc0 - 2 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • dad9c98d - bittorrent: decode extension bits in handshake
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/26083/diffs?diff_id=1950198595&start_sha=32e0c320dba360234b04a1e93285469586a8daad)

I figured out the one frequently seen bit that wasn't covered in the previous version, so now all the common bits are dissected and the rest get dissected as unassigned. That group could potentially be split into one group with bits that have been seen but whose function is unknown, and a group with bits that haven't been seen, but I'm not sure if that adds any real value.

Also sorted the fields so they appear left-to-right.
added this merge request to the [merge train](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_trains) at position 2
